claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Alex being 8 years old means he meets the age requirement (under 16).

Now I have a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you!

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards his clothes, food, and things he needs - I give about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. Since Alex lives with someone else, I have a couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to ensure I have the full picture:

**Is Alex currently in local council care, hospital, or residential accommodation? Or does he live with a friend or relative in an informal arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He just lives with his mum in a normal arrangement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying.

One final question:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance where he lives with his mum?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. It's just a normal living arrangement with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- Alex lives with his mum, not with you
- You contribute approximately £30 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, food, etc.)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance ✓

The current Child Benefit rate for the eldest or only child is £25.60 per week. Since you're contributing £30 per week, which is **more** than the Child Benefit amount, you meet the requirement to be considered "responsible" for Alex even though he doesn't live with you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Alex is under 16** – He's 8 years old, so he meets the age requirement.

✅ **You live in the UK** – This is a key eligibility requirement.

✅ **You're considered responsible for Alex** – Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you contribute £30 per week towards his upkeep. This is more than the Child Benefit rate (currently £25.60 per week for an only/eldest child), which means you qualify as being "responsible" for him under the rules.

✅ **No one else is claiming** – Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at a time, and currently no one else is claiming for Alex.

✅ **No local council involvement** – The council isn't paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

**Important note:** Since Alex lives with his mum, she may also be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child. If both of you wish to claim, you should agree between yourselves who will receive it. If you cannot agree, HMRC will decide.

You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit if you wish. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
